content.scenario: A consumer files a complaint with the Central Authority alleging that a company is engaging in unfair trade practices by selling defective products. The Central Authority conducts a preliminary inquiry and finds a prima facie case of violation of consumer rights.
content.outcome: The Central Authority must cause an investigation to be made into the matter by the Director-General or the District Collector, as it is satisfied that there exists a prima facie case of violation of consumer rights.

user_queries: What happens when the Central Authority finds a prima facie case of consumer rights violation?
Can the Central Authority conduct an investigation on its own?
How does the Central Authority handle complaints of unfair trade practices?
